Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Data Protection Law enacted 2023, establishing the Data Protection Authority (DPA) as national trust layer. Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009 of 2023) enacted. National Communications Act (October 2017) provides telecoms regulation. Draft bills on Electronic Transactions, Cybersecurity, and Cybercrime are before Parliament. GovStack notes 'no enabling legislation for data sharing and data analysis yet' but the Data Protection Law provides foundational framework.
revision_notes: Fetched both cited sources plus a World Bank digital economy diagnostic. GovStack (Sep 2024, on-point Somalia primary source, despite a Rwanda-slugged URL) states explicitly there is 'no enabling legislation for data sharing and data analysis yet'. The World Bank diagnostic confirms Somalia still lacks an overarching Government Enterprise Architecture and a shared interoperability solution; data remain hosted separately by individual MDAs with no common technical or legal standard for exchange. The Data Protection Act (2023) and ID Act (2023), cited as the basis for the original score of 3 (Yes), govern personal data protection and identity registration respectively - not cross-government data-exchange authority specifically, which is the variable being scored. Electronic Transactions, Cybersecurity and Cybercrime bills remain in progress (Cybercrime Bill completed only its First Reading in Parliament, December 2025, per MOCT). Revised down from 3 (Yes) to 2 (Under development): the legal building blocks are in progress but no dedicated data-exchange enabling legislation has been enacted.
revised_comments: Somalia has enacted foundational digital-economy laws - the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023) and the Identification and Registration Act (Law No. 009 of 2023) - but no primary legislation yet specifically establishes authority for cross-government data sharing or governs a data exchange system. Government assessments note that ministries, departments and agencies lack a shared Government Enterprise Architecture or interoperability platform, with data hosted separately by individual agencies rather than exchanged through common standards. Draft Electronic Transactions, Cybersecurity and Cybercrime bills are progressing through Parliament - the Cybercrime Bill completed its First Reading in December 2025 - but none has yet been enacted. Enabling legislation for data exchange is therefore under development rather than in force.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Data Protection Law 2023 allows cross-border data transfers based on adequacy, contractual safeguards, or consent. DPA established. National Data Center planned (operational early 2026) to consolidate critical applications. Horn of Africa Initiative notes 'framework remains at an early stage, with further regulatory guidance and institutional capacity needed.' Limited but developing controls.
revision_notes: Fetched the original HoAI background paper and LinkedIn source, then verified via the official Somalia Data Protection Authority (SDPA) site, the Act's text, a January 2026 news report on the approved implementing regulation, and a June 2026 peer-reviewed analysis of Somali data sovereignty. Chapter VI (Articles 30-31) of the Data Protection Act sets out a detailed cross-border transfer regime requiring an adequacy assessment, contractual/consent-based safeguards, and record-keeping by data controllers - a fairly comprehensive legal framework, further reinforced by SDPA-issued cross-border transfer guidance and a Regulatory Framework approved by the Council of Ministers in January 2026. However, the peer-reviewed source finds enforcement and institutional capacity still nascent - the SDPA only completed its first training of public/private institutions on the law in June 2026 - and highlights Somalia's continued structural dependence on externally hosted cloud infrastructure, meaning practical control over data has not yet been established. This profile matches 'Strong yet unenforced controls' (3) rather than 'Limited controls' (2); revised up one level accordingly.
revised_comments: Somalia's Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023) sets out a comprehensive cross-border data transfer regime (Chapter VI), requiring data controllers to assess the adequacy of protection in the receiving jurisdiction, or rely on contractual safeguards or data-subject consent, before transferring personal data abroad, together with record-keeping obligations. The Somalia Data Protection Authority has since issued specific guidance on cross-border transfer rules, and in January 2026 the Council of Ministers approved a Regulatory Framework implementing the Act. Enforcement capacity remains nascent, however: the Authority only completed its first training of public and private institutions on the law in mid-2026, and independent analysis highlights Somalia's continued structural dependence on externally hosted cloud infrastructure, meaning practical control over government data has yet to be fully established. The legal controls are therefore strong on paper but not yet consistently enforced.
